_about: The Magic Portals port's carrancas - the wall-mounted stone gargoyles that spit
fireballs, which Enhanced's role table calls 'turret' (entity_roles.json:226).
The original never uses that word: its entities are carranca.ent and
carranca_right.ent, and its script is ETHCallback_carranca.angelscript.
Every number here is DECODED except the cull margin, which is marked. The
Godot project's hazards.json carries its own turret block marked _guess with a speed of
180 px/s and a life of 4 s; both are inventions, and the original's own
fireball.ent states the speed outright. See

_source: the original's fireball.ent: CustomData speed 130 and teleportable 1,
Collision 16 x 16, shape 2, sensor 1, bullet 1, density 0, restitution 0,
static 0, <Scale> 1.2. Its gravityScale is 1 in the file and addFireball sets
it to 0 at spawn (bytes 417483..417923), so a fireball flies flat and never falls.
radius_px: shape 2 is BS_CIRCLE (ETHEntityProperties.h:96), whose radius is
(size.x + size.y) / 4 of the collision box (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:56-62) after
the box is scaled by the entity's scale (:73), which is its <Scale> 1.2 times the
spawn's own scale (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:61; addFireball's g_scale, one level unit):
(16 + 16) / 4 x 1.2 = 9.6 units. The converter builds every other body by the
same rule (tscn.py _collider_lines).
A SENSOR, but a DYNAMIC one (static 0, ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:68), so Box2D
begins a contact with every body it overlaps and ETHBeginContactCallback_fireball
(listing L85862) decides what that does: it passes a carranca, a sensor (all but
a shock_agent, which it destroys with itself) and a character when its
killMainCharacter is clear; ANYTHING ELSE - a wall, a closed door, a crate, a
stone, a barrel, a minion - destroys it (#146-152), and is then burned if it is
burnable and exploded if it is explosive (#159-188). So a fireball dies on the
first solid thing it touches; footage F6 #72 shows one stopping on 2-12's
closed door. (Until planning step 114 this file read sensor 1 as 'nothing stops
it', and the port's fireballs flew through walls. That was wrong.)
It has no <Sprite>. What is seen is its ParticleSystem (explosion.JPG) and
its Light, so the layer has no image to draw it with.
_portal_source: WHERE A FIREBALL IS IN A PORTAL (planning step 135, the backlog's G6). fireball.ent says
finds one through getObjectInPortal (357583..358053, #1-11): an EntityGrabber round the
portal's point with PortalManager.portalCollisionRadius, which the constructor sets to
14 x getScale (135924..136705, #106-113). For a circle body the grabber
(EntityGrabber::EntityGrabber, 23924..24990, #65-105) takes an entity whose point is
closer than GetCollisionBox().size.x x scale(0.5) + that radius, a strict compare.
GetCollisionBox returns the entity's box UNSCALED (ETHEntity.cpp:314-321; only
CreateBody scales it, ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:72-73), so the fireball's share is half
its 16 x 16 box, 8 units, not its 9.6 body: in a portal while its centre is within
8 + 14 = 22 units of the portal's. portal_grab_px is that 8.

_source: carrancaCallback (ETHCallback_carranca.angelscript, bytes 416779..417483).
elapsedTime is seeded from the node's startStride the first time the callback
runs, gathers getLastFrameElapsedTime every frame, and when it PASSES the
node's stride the carranca calls addFireball and resets elapsedTime to ZERO.
So the first shot comes stride - startStride ms after the level starts, and
one every stride ms after that. The reset is to zero rather than a
subtraction, so a long frame does not carry its overshoot into the next shot.
The Godot project reads startStride as an initial DELAY instead and then fires every
stride (hazards.gd:346-349), which on a node whose startStride is 0 - every
carranca in level0a is - fires at once instead of a stride later. The decoded
script wins over the Godot project's reading, as the acceptance rule has it.
Both are bare uints with no speed field, which is what proves they are
milliseconds. default_ms is only for a node that names no stride; every
placement in the game names one.

_note: A carranca fires along its node's (dirX, dirY). carrancaCallback builds
vector2(dirX, dirY) and hands it to addFireball, which stores it on the
fireball as 'dir'.
NOT a unit vector in the data: level0a's carranca_right_ent_792 carries
dirX = 1.2, and eight of the game's 28 carrancas carry one that is not 1
(0.7 to 2; out/parity/program/G6/carrancas.txt). The port normalised, as the
Godot project does, until planning step 149.
BUILT in planning step 149 (program wave 3a, G4; step 135 found it and left it, saying it
retimed every carranca): ETHCallback_fireball (bytes 418524..418930) reads 'dir' back every
frame: #1-13 GetVector2('dir'), #15-24 GetFloat('speed'), #25-43 AddToPositionXY(dir x
scaledUnitsPerSecond(speed)), with nothing normalising it on the way (carrancaCallback builds
vector2(dirX, dirY), addFireball #58-67 SetVector2s it as it is, listing L85539). So the
original's fireball flies at |dir| x 130, and so does the port's: the turret keeps the node's
(dirX, dirY) as written, and a fireball's velocity is that times fireball.speed_px_s. 1.2 x
130 = 156 units/s on 2-01 (level0a), 1.25 on 2-03 (level2a), 1.6 on 2-07 (level6a), -1.3 and 2
on 2-15 (level14a), 1.2 on 2-18 (level17a) and 2-28 (level27a), 0.7 on 4-13 (level12c); the
other 20 carrancas carry a unit dir and fly at 130, as does every converted shot
(burnProjectile hands addFireball the shot's unit 'direction') and the dragons'. In wall time
at 60 Hz each is 0.96 of that, the script clock's floor (clock.json): 2-01's fireball covers
2.496 units a tick.
A fireball dies on the first solid thing it touches (the fireball block above),
so a flight ends at a wall almost everywhere. One that leaves the level without
touching anything - over an open edge - would fly for ever, so it is dropped once
it leaves the level's bounds by this margin, which is how the beholder's spikes
are dropped (boss.json). A safety net, not the end of a flight: the original's
flies on off the scene, and what Ethanon does with it there is not decoded.
